column1: # The metric names the retired server publishes, the old backlog.
# Columns: name, instrument, unit, attributes, whether a helper that records it
# has a caller, description. A unit of - is an instrument declared without one.
# Read from a run, not from the source. The binary was built with
# `-tags "full mqtt mqttbroker observability sqlite"` and CGO_ENABLED=1, started
# observability.metrics.enabled and its prometheus exporter both true, and
# scraped at GET /metrics. One simulated CORE One dialled the printer listener,
# one authenticated GET /api/printers was made, one was refused, and the printer
# 11 of these 18 names appeared on that scrape:
# instrument reaches a Prometheus scrape only once it has recorded, so a name
# absent from that list is one no dashboard on this deployment ever drew.
# The recorded column is coarser than the scrape: it says a helper touching the
# instrument is called somewhere under legacy/. api_request_errors_total is
# recorded by that measure and needs a status of 400 or more from the one call
# site, which is GET /api/printers at legacy/transport/httpapi/handlers.go:174.
# Three names are never-recorded because RecordCommandSent and
# RecordCommandExecuted have no caller anywhere in the tree. A dashboard built
# on commands_total has always drawn nothing.
# printer_id sits on queue_command_duration_seconds and command_duration_seconds,
# which are histograms. An earlier design decision forbids exactly that label on a
# histogram, and the scrape above carried it.
# Nothing in the core answers any of these names. The core's own /metrics
# carries pcl_* names and the overlap is zero, which docs/CHANGELOG.md records
# as a loss rather than a migration.
